- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.5+), especially in early forecast horizon (1-3 days).
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment (e.g., -1.0+), particularly in mid-to-late forecast (7-15 days).
- Avoid overreacting to recent price volatility; model tends to overshoot after sharp moves (e.g., +7.0+ or -7.0+ in 30d forecast).
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Lagged sentiment effects: if sentiment was positive 3-5 days ago, model often overcorrects; if negative, undercorrects — adjust forecast by -0.5 to +0.5 of sentiment magnitude.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts often overestimate early in the period (days 1-5) when sentiment is volatile; reduce by 2-5% if sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- Don’t ignore recent true values — if last 3 days show downward trend, reduce forecast slope even if sentiment is positive.
